'''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka City|qq=}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]].

== Deities ==
The current enshrined deities are as follows:<ref name="神社庁">[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association).</ref>
* [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
* [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
* [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社.

According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined.

== History ==
The exact date of establishment is unknown.

The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake'').

In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods.

During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]].
